Posted April 25, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
For the most part, I was very pleased with the NORML conference last week in San Francisco.
See
 Canadian Senator Stars At NORML Conference As DEAland Threatens Retaliation, Again. Rightwing Think Tank Cited As Semi-Official Source. Is Canada Still Too White To Invade? Bad Neighbor Policy?
and
 A Good Friday Moment At the NORML Conference. Why I Do This.

However, I was bemused when a good friend (female) handed me a little 4x5 inch piece of yellow paper that someone had printed up.

On one side it said, The arrest rate for African Americans is 2 ½ times the arrest rate of white Americans. The number of African American Speakers at the conference? Zero? Is this NORML?

The other side read: Speaker Count: Men 60 Women 11. Is this NORML?

I told my friend that when I became National Director of NORML in 1992 I said that it was the whitest organization that I had belonged to that didn't have a golf course. Despite our longstanding efforts, that is still the case.

In fact, there were only a very few non-white faces in the audience.

(Forgive me, but I just cannot resist pointing out the inconsistency of the logic on the flyer: If more African Americans are supposed to be there because they are arrested at 2 ½ times the rates for whites, then the ratio of male to female speakers would be just about right because males get arrested far more often than females. And men [yes, disproportionately black] are vastly over-represented in prisons. But that had nothing to do with any of it.)

First, the reason that there were not more women speakers begins with the fact that there are far more male than female activists in the anti-prohibitionist movement. That is not NORML's fault. Men outnumber women by substantial margins in almost all areas of politics.

Second, many women who were asked were unable to attend, for personal reasons, or because they could not afford to come. (NORML is not able to pay expenses for speakers, and women inevitably have more family obligations.)

Others who did attend, declined to be on panels for various reasons.

Nonetheless, it seemed to be assumed that NORML had been sexist in its choice of speakers. Ironically, this rush to judgement was most egregiously expressed by a participant on the panel on Women and the Drug War. She objected that a prominent female activist who was present in the audience should have been on that panel. What she did not know was that this woman had been asked and had declined for personal reasons, and suggested the woman who was outraged that her friend was not on the panel!

A number of prominent women have also been asked to sit on the NORML Board and/or Advisory Board, but they have declined, for various reasons. The fact is that such women are much sought-after for such boards and have to choose where they will serve. NORML loses out to other causes about which women feel strongly, such as women's rights, etc. That is hardly surprising.

(One happy exception to this is ACLU President Nadine Strossen, who serves as co-chair of the Advisory Board. She was the featured speaker at the Conference Lunch, and is just extraordinarily brilliant.)

Even in staffing, NORML has problems recruiting women. One ad for an important staff position was allowed to run an extra two weeks in hopes that a woman would apply. NONE did. That is not NORML's fault.

My point is simply that outraged demands that NORML be more gender-inclusive should have at least been delayed until it was determined why there were not more women speaking.

The absence of non-whites is another matter, but I truly wish that we white males were to blame.

The simple fact is that the leaders of the black and Hispanic communities are not only overwhelmingly prohibitionist, they also seem to be utterly indifferent to the plight of their own people in prisons. One exception to this is NORML Board member Clifford W. Thornton, Jr., the only African American on the Board at present.

The racist origins of marijuana prohibition are well known to anyone active in the reform movement, but not it seems to the so-called leaders of the Black and Mexican American communities. Lock my people up! seems to be their motto.

When I was speaking at the conference on my panel on international developments, I ranted about the devastating impact of the suppression of medical cannabis in Africa, especially in the context of the AIDS epidemic.
See
 The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs Resolution on the Control of Cannabis in Africa. UN Narks Urge War on Poorest of the Poor. Cannabis Prohibition Does Most Damage In Poor Countries.

I pointed out the irony of someone as white as I am having to say this, but you can listen forever and hear almost nothing about it from the professional AFRICAN-American leaders. And I really do hope that this offends these hustlers.

Now there are two serious points here.

First, NORML is not just inclusive, it is desperately inclusive. It needs everyone it can get, especially qualified females and minority members, but it really cannot afford to recruit the unwilling. Its job is to end cannabis prohibition, not to implement the feminist agenda or to appear to be politically correct.

Second, and much more important, the absence of people of color is the result of a serious problem in DEAland, and not because NORML is a branch of the KKK.

Whites created marijuana prohibition as a tool for the suppression of racial minorities, and it would appear that whites will have to end it to save ourselves and our country without the help of many of the intended victims.

There is an awful irony there.

And, by the way, the phrase The White Man's Burden is Rudyard Kipling's.

It was printed in McClure's magazine in 1899.

It may seem quaint and both racist and imperialist today. But it also seems relevant to the various wars at hand. The point of all of this is that the best of motives do not guarantee justice, but an old-fashioned sense of obligation may bring about needed change.

Take up the White Man's burden--
Send forth the best ye breed--
Go, bind your sons to exile
To serve your captives' need;
To wait, in heavy harness,
On fluttered folk and wild--
Your new-caught sullen peoples,
Half devil and half child.
Take up the White Man's burden--
In patience to abide,
To veil the threat of terror
And check the show of pride;
By open speech and simple,
An hundred times made plain,
To seek another's profit
And work another's gain.
Take up the White Man's burden--
The savage wars of peace--
Fill full the mouth of Famine,
And bid the sickness cease;
And when your goal is nearest
(The end for others sought)
Watch sloth and heathen folly
Bring all your hope to nought.
Take up the White Man's burden--
No iron rule of kings,
But toil of serf and sweeper--
The tale of common things.
The ports ye shall not enter,
The roads ye shall not tread,
Go, make them with your living
And mark them with your dead.
Take up the White Man's burden,
And reap his old reward--
The blame of those ye better
The hate of those ye guard--
The cry of hosts ye humour
(Ah, slowly!) toward the light:--
" Why brought ye us from bondage,
Our loved Egyptian night? "
Take up the White Man's burden--
Ye dare not stoop to less--
Nor call too loud on Freedom
To cloak your weariness.
By all ye will or whisper,
By all ye leave or do,
The silent sullen peoples
Shall weigh your God and you.
Take up the White Man's burden!
Have done with childish days--
The lightly-proffered laurel,
The easy ungrudged praise:
Comes now, to search your manhood
Through all the thankless years,
Cold, edged with dear-bought wisdom,
The judgment of your peers.
(MarijuanaNews note: The opinions in this poem are those of Mr. Kipling and not necessarily those of the management.)
